basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Duxerunt autem Abram et Nachor uxores. Nomen uxoris Abram Sarai, et nomen uxoris Nachor'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Duxerunt autem Abram et Nachor uxores. Nomen uxoris Abram Sarai, et nomen uxoris Nachor Melcha, filia Aran patris Melchae et patris Jeschae. Dicunt majores nostri Jescham hanc ipsam esse Saram uxorem Abrahae, quia videlicet iidem fratres germani Abraham et Nachor duas sorores filias Aran uxores habuerint. Quod si ita est, non potest Aran pater earumdem idem intelligi qui fuit frater junior Abrahae et Nachor, sed alter ejusdem nominis homo. Constat enim quia Abraham decem solum annis Saram conjugem suam praecessit, dicente ipso coram Domino: Putasne centenario nascetur filius, et Sara nonagenaria pariet filium (Genes. XVII, 37)? Et quomodo frater ejus junior potuit habere filiam, quae illo decem annis minor esset, se autem ipso septem aut non amplius quam octo?
